contract: Musoq Search scope and path semantics
implementationStatus: Design only. These rules must be implemented and verified against the actual filesystem in later scopes.

security.containmentCheck: before convenience filters and before content reads
security.lexicalContainment: normalize separators and dot segments, then require the candidate path to equal the root or have the root plus a separator as prefix
security.physicalContainment: when links are followed, resolve the target and require it to remain under the resolved physical root
security.outsideRoot: reject as a containment violation; outside-root candidates cannot be made safe by an include, ignore or hidden rule
security.pathIdentity: retain each eligible path identity; do not use convenience filtering as a security boundary

rootResolution.relativeRoot: resolve against the query working directory captured in the execution request
rootResolution.absoluteRoot: normalize without changing the requested filesystem object
rootResolution.rootFile: the single file is the complete candidate set when it is eligible
rootResolution.rootDirectory: the directory is the traversal boundary
rootResolution.missingRoot: typed failure before an empty scan can be reported

traversal.nonRecursive: inspect only the root directory's direct eligible files
traversal.directoryPruning: prune only a directory explicitly excluded by a security decision or an explicit directory-only exclusion; file extension includes never prune a directory whose descendants may match
traversal.regularFiles: only regular files become path/content candidates; special entries are policy decisions, not silently regular files
traversal.determinism: record normalized relative paths and sort the resolved candidate manifest ordinally for the fingerprint; SQL result order still requires ORDER BY

includeExclude.include: when non-empty, a file must match at least one include glob; an unmatched directory is still traversed when a descendant could match
includeExclude.exclude: a matching exclude glob denies the path after include evaluation; excludes win over includes
includeExclude.directoryRules: a directory-only exclusion may prune descendants; a file extension pattern alone may not
includeExclude.negation: negated ignore rules are evaluated within their ignore source and precedence; they cannot cross the security containment boundary

ignorePolicy.parentDirectory: a pruned ignored directory is not reopened solely because a descendant negation exists; the parent must be re-included before the descendant can be considered
ignorePolicy.fingerprint: record every loaded ignore source, its normalized path, precedence and SHA-256 content hash

hidden.explicitEnable: include hidden files/directories after security checks

links.default: do not follow symbolic links or reparse-point directories
links.followEnabled: resolve physical targets, enforce physical containment and maintain a visited physical-directory set to stop cycles
links.outsideTarget: reject or report according to the explicit link policy; never treat it as in-root by lexical spelling

hardLinks.default: each directory entry path is a separate path candidate, even when file identity is shared
hardLinks.deduplication: no inode/file-ID deduplication in the path contract

inaccessible.descendantDefault: fail with the path and phase recorded
inaccessible.explicitSkip: permitted only as a named policy whose skipped count and completeness are surfaced by the audit contract

scopeFingerprint.canonicalization: object keys sorted ordinally, arrays retain semantic order, compact separators, no implicit machine-specific fields
scopeFingerprint.explanation: retain the normalized policy, loaded rule hashes, candidate counts and per-path decision reasons needed to reproduce the digest
scopeFingerprint.sharedDocs: examples use synthetic relative roots; actual absolute machine paths belong only in ignored local evidence

fixtures.reason: nested higher-scope rules and negation are applied without changing containment
a pruned parent is not reopened by a descendant negation
shared physical file identity does not collapse distinct path rows
